name: coldframe
cost: Free (MIT). Hosting it costs whatever your server costs
works_with: Python 3 standard library; podman or Docker for deployment
short: A honeypot that poses as a supermarket fridge controller and logs who connects, the passwords they try and the exploits they use.
what: coldframe pretends to be an internet-facing refrigeration supervisor, either a Danfoss AK-SM 800A or a Copeland/Dixell XWEB EVO. It copies what scanners see on real units, lets weak logins succeed onto a fake dashboard, and tags requests that match public exploits by CVE. Every request goes to a JSON log, and nothing the attacker does is real. It is one Python file with no dependencies outside the standard library.
who: Security researchers and defenders who want to watch attacks on refrigeration controllers. You need to be comfortable running and locking down a public server. It does not protect real controllers.
needs: For a public decoy: a server (the README suggests an Ubuntu 24.04 droplet) and rootful podman or Docker
A provider firewall where you can limit SSH to your own address

steps.title: Try it locally
steps.text: Open http://localhost:8080. Every request shows up as a JSON line on stdout and in `events.jsonl`.

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.text: They start the honeypot on loopback and attack it.

steps.title: Quickest deploy
steps.text: Create an Ubuntu 24.04 server and paste `cloud-init.yaml` into the User data box. Change `PERSONA=danfoss` to `dixell` for the XWEB persona. About two minutes after boot it listens on port 80 (and 443 for Danfoss). Then allow only the decoy's ports from anywhere and SSH from your own address.

steps.title: Or build the container yourself
steps.text: Each build makes a fresh self-signed certificate. Podman needs a UID range for `--userns=auto`, once per host.
steps.code:
podman build -t coldframe .
echo "containers:2147483647:2147483648" | sudo tee -a /etc/subuid /etc/subgid

steps.title: Run it
steps.text: Use rootful podman or Docker. Rootless port forwarding makes every attacker look like the same internal IP. For Modbus, add `-e MODBUS_PORT=5020 -p 502:5020`.
steps.code:
sudo podman run -d --name coldframe --restart=always \
  --read-only --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --userns=auto \
  --memory 128m --pids-limit 512 --log-opt max-size=10m \
  -p 80:8080 -p 443:8443 \
  -v coldframe-logs:/logs:U \
  -e PERSONA=danfoss \
  coldframe

try.label: From the README
try.text: Start the Danfoss persona locally, open http://localhost:8080, log in with the weak login `Supervisor` / `12345`, press a defrost button, and watch the `login_attempt` and `control` events appear in `events.jsonl`.

watch: You are putting a server on the internet to attract attackers. Expose only the ports the persona would really have, block outbound traffic except DNS and package updates, and keep SSH open only to your own address.
Log fields come from attackers. Treat them as untrusted when you view or process them.
The code is public, so anyone can fingerprint its exact responses. The README suggests changing the persona strings, page layout and certificate subject for your deployment.
Some scanners flag industrial devices on cloud IPs as likely honeypots.
The vendor favicon and Danfoss start page are not included. Point `FAVICON_FILE` or `INDEX_FILE` at copies only if you have the right to use them, and only on private deployments.
